source.title: Training Tips for the Transformer Model

record.file_problem: Full text provided; no apparent truncation or corruption that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Tests batch-size effects on held-out translation quality in English-to-Czech NMT, extending batch-size generalization findings to a different task and model family.
record.gate_note: The study reports held-out BLEU learning curves for batch-size comparisons. Its main comparison is by time and processed examples, not at a fixed epoch budget; it does not measure a training-to-test error gap directly.
record.test_reason: The study tests batch-size effects on held-out translation quality in a new setting. Section 4.5 explicitly states that BASE's larger-batch advantage persists when comparing equal numbers of processed examples, which supplies an approximate equal-epoch comparison on the same dataset.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: larger batches improve BASE's BLEU learning curves with diminishing returns; BIG needs a minimum batch size for stable training, with little difference among sufficiently large single-GPU batches. The authors also recommend using more GPUs and explain the implicit learning-rate scaling in their default schedule.
record.recipe_differences: English-to-Czech Transformer NMT; batch-size comparisons use held-out BLEU learning curves and time/examples to score, rather than fixed-epoch image-classification or language-model comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch-size effects differed between BASE and BIG; for BIG, 1450 trained well while 1400 dropped off after two hours.
record.problems: The relevant outcomes are BLEU learning curves rather than a directly measured train-test error gap. Batch-size comparisons are not reported at fixed epochs. Some plotted curves lack exact numerical values in the text; authors note no proper significance evaluation for checkpoint-averaging effects, not these batch-size comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant batch-size outcomes with text-reported values were omitted; other batch-size curves are displayed in Figures 5 and 6.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers under different tuning regimes.

The specified image-classification and language-model benchmarks; a harmful large-batch threshold; controlled tests of longer training, normalization, or regularization as remedies; equal-epoch outcomes for the single-GPU BIG comparisons.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

missing.what: BIG multi-GPU batch scaling: BLEU 25.6 requires more than 9000M processed subwords on one GPU, 4644M on two, 2706M on six, and 2728M on eight, with batch size 1500 per GPU. These outcomes are absent from the rows and rows_left_out.

The step-based inverse-square-root schedule implicitly increases the post-warmup learning rate at equal processed-example counts by the square root of the effective batch-size multiplier. This conditions interpretation of the multi-GPU results as an adapted recipe.

record.verdict_notes: Held-out BLEU is sufficient for the held-out-performance component of V5; a measured training–test gap is unnecessary. Equal processed-subword budgets approximate equal epochs on the same training data. The study is not an original source. Its findings qualify extension to Transformer translation rather than directly contradicting the specified benchmark results.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer held-out performance under tuning regimes.
Fixed-epoch comparisons; image classifiers and language models; normalization or regularization changes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other measures of the generalization gap.
Removal of memorized examples and resulting held-out accuracy.

rows.subject: BASE
rows.operation_detail: Compared held-out BLEU learning curves across batch sizes on one GPU.
rows.measure: Held-out BLEU; time and examples till BLEU 18 are described in text.
rows.baseline: batch_size=1500: about 3 days and 2260M examples to get over BLEU 18
rows.value: batch_size=3000: 7 hours and 260M examples to get over BLEU 18
rows.note: This is a wall-clock/examples comparison, not a fixed-epoch comparison; authors say larger batch sizes up to 4500 are clearly better for BLEU.
rows.check: The numerical values are correct, but 'examples' means processed subwords. The record overlooks the authors' explicit statement that the larger-batch BLEU advantage persists at equal processed-example budgets.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.5, Figure 5 and footnote 24; Section 2.3 defines examples as processed subwords.

rows.subject: BASE
rows.operation_detail: Compared held-out BLEU learning curves across batch sizes on one GPU.
rows.measure: Held-out BLEU; time and examples till BLEU 18 are described in text.
rows.baseline: batch_size=3000: 7 hours and 260M examples to get over BLEU 18
rows.value: batch_size=1500: about 3 days and 2260M examples to get over BLEU 18
rows.note: Authors report this smaller batch needed about 10 times longer and 9 times more examples; not a fixed-epoch comparison.
rows.check: This duplicates R1 with the comparator direction swapped; it is not independent evidence. Smaller batches require substantially more processed subwords to exceed BLEU 18.

rows.subject: BIG
rows.operation_detail: Compared held-out BLEU learning curves across batch sizes on one GPU.
rows.note: Text says batch size 1450 trains well; exact BLEU values are only in the figure.
rows.check: The text establishes stable training at 1450 versus instability at 1400, but Figure 6 compares wall-clock time. This row does not establish their relative BLEU at equal processed-example budgets.

rows.subject: BIG
rows.operation_detail: Compared held-out BLEU learning curves across batch sizes on one GPU.
rows.note: Text says this run drops off after two hours and recovers only slowly; larger batches did not make BLEU worse in the reported BIG experiments.
rows.check: The temporary collapse and slow recovery at batch size 1400 are stated explicitly, so the value need not remain 'figure only'. This duplicates R3's comparison and does not establish an equal-epoch effect.

relationships.condition: Single-GPU BASE English-to-Czech Transformer training, batch sizes 1500 versus 3000 subwords
relationships.reason: R1 and R2 show larger batches reaching BLEU 18 with 260M rather than 2260M processed subwords; the text explicitly says the advantage persists at equal example budgets. This qualifies extension to translation without establishing a harmful-batch threshold.
relationships.display_finding: The larger batch reached BLEU 18 after 260M rather than 2260M processed subwords, with an advantage also reported at equal processed-example budgets rather than exactly matched epochs.
